mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM642 engine for the S 320 CDI costs £2,200-£3,500 supply-only; a rebuilt OM642 BlueTEC engine for the S 350 CDI costs £2,500-£4,300 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start or intermittent starting problems are the classic warning signs on the OM642 engine. One owner reported an OM642 engine seizing at 120,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI engine (OM642) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 is fundamentally robust, but S Class owners should be aware of timing chain stretch and oil cooler seal degradation. With these addressed, the engine is capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 320 CDI and S 350 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is needed.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £2,200-£3,500 - comparable to the value of a £4,000-£15,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5-9.5 litres with filter.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 320 CDI/350 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 320 CDI launched with the W221 generation in 2005 as Mercedes' flagship diesel, powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel producing 235hp. The S 350 CDI joined the range using the same OM642 V6 architecture, with outputs ranging from 235hp to 258hp in later BlueTEC form. In 2009, the facelift W221 introduced BlueTEC technology with AdBlue SCR systems, improving emissions compliance. Both variants continued through to 2013 when the W222 generation replaced them.

milestones.description: OM642.930, 3.0L V6 diesel, 235hp @ 3,600rpm (S 320 CDI, W221 launch)
OM642.862, 3.0L V6 BlueTEC diesel, 258hp (S 350 CDI BlueTEC, facelift W221)
End of W221 production; replaced by S 350 BlueTEC in W222 generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 320 CDI/350 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S 320 CDI and S 350 CDI's OM642 V6 diesel is a refined and durable engine, but it has well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. Timing chain stretch, oil cooler seal degradation, and BlueTEC AdBlue system issues are the most common failure patterns driving replacement decisions. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure - The S 320/350 CDI's Most Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch and plastic guides to wear. This is a known issue on the OM642 V6. One owner reported an OM642 engine seizing at 120,000 miles. Intermittent starting problems have also been traced to stretched timing chains causing cam and crank sensor misalignment.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: STAR diagnostic, cam/crank correlation check, borescope inspection
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether chain is stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles if caught before chain stretches significantly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2005-2013 S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI is worth approximately £4,000-£15,000 depending on mileage and condition. These flagship saloons have suffered significant depreciation, meaning replacement costs can approach or exceed vehicle value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start or experience intermittent starting problems on your S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI, act immediately. A stretched timing chain on the OM642 can cause catastrophic engine failure. Specialist timing chain replacement at £1,800-£2,800 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has already jumped, a full rebuilt OM642 engine is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes S 320 CDI/350 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Degradation - Coolant Contamination Risk
problems.rootCause: The OM642's oil cooler seals degrade under repeated thermal cycles, allowing oil to leak into the coolant system. This is a labour-intensive repair requiring removal of the intake manifold to access the cooler in the V of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace seals, flush cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete unit swap with upgraded cooler seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If coolant contamination has caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical S 320/350 CDI is worth £4,000-£15,000.
problems.recommendation: If you notice milky coolant or oil contamination on your S 320 CDI or S 350 CDI, have the oil cooler seals inspected immediately. Specialist seal replacement at £950-£1,400 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the engine has been run with contaminated oil, a full rebuilt OM642 is the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM642 oil cooler seal replacement & rebuilt engines

problems.h4: OM642 BlueTEC AdBlue System Failure - The S 350 CDI BlueTEC's Emissions Challenge
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue SCR system can suffer from injector clogging due to urea crystallisation, triggering countdown warnings and eventual engine start prevention. NOx sensor failures and DPF saturation on short-journey driving patterns are also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan of SCR system, tank, dosing module, NOx sensors
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms which component has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue injector, flush tank and lines, reset SCR counter
repairOptions.longevity: If injector is blocked beyond cleaning

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tank, dosing module, NOx sensors and update ECU software
repairOptions.longevity: Comprehensive emissions fix; removes start limits

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete unit swap with new AdBlue components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If emissions issues have caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2013 S 350 CDI BlueTEC is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue faults are primarily emission-system issues, not core mechanical failures. If your S 350 CDI BlueTEC runs smoothly but displays emissions warnings, a specialist SCR overhaul is significantly cheaper and entirely sufficient. However, if the fault has triggered repeated limp modes, the DPF and turbo may be compromised. In that scenario, a rebuilt engine with integrated emission components provides a complete reset.
